## How the Agents tab works today

Facts from internal/tui/agents_screen.go, internal/tui/tui.go, and internal/tui/health.go:
- The tab starts with stopped agents hidden. h shows them and hides them again. The pod note says 'h shows N stopped' or 'h hides N stopped'.
- hideable() covers a stopped card and a stale card.
- The manager card is the one exemption: the pod code picks the manager and places it without the hidden check. That is the rule from task 129: manager cards stay visible.
- Every card of a pod hangs on the manager card as the tree anchor.
- The Health tab already hides stopped cards, managers included, with no exemption.

Today, hive with one stopped manager:

  Agents
  ┌ home ─────────┐  ┌ hive ────────────┐
  │ coordinator ● │  │ manager-hive ○   │
  └───────────────┘  └──────────────────┘

You want the hive column gone, like a stopped worker.

## 1. What shows for a project with no live card?

When the manager hides, the pod loses its tree anchor.

  A: pod gone                     B: empty stub
  ┌ home ─────────┐               ┌ home ─────────┐ ┌ hive ────────────┐
  │ coordinator ● │               │ coordinator ● │ │ hive · empty     │
  └───────────────┘               └───────────────┘ └──────────────────┘

| Choice | Answer | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (REC) | The pod disappears when every card in it is stopped. h shows every hidden pod again. | Only live work on the tab. Matches your rule. You can browse with h without starting anything. | Agents no longer lists all projects at once |
| B | The pod stays as an empty column with the title and the note 'h shows 1 stopped' | Every project stays visible | The tab still lists every project, which is what you dislike, only smaller |

## 2. The rare case: a stopped manager with a live child

Example: a worker respawned after its manager stopped.

| Choice | Answer | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (REC) | The manager card hides. The pod keeps its border, and the children hang from the pod top border, like the home pod draws a tree without a manager today | One rule for every stopped card | One more tree shape to draw and test |
| B | The manager card stays while a child is live | The tree keeps its anchor | A stopped card can still show up |

## Your confirm step: interrogate round 3

**How it works today.** In an ask card you pick with arrows, space, 1..5, or a click, tab adds a note, and enter on the last question sends the card at once. There is no look-before-send. The a1 card today showed the cost: the card sent, you said "stop that was not right", and the fix cost a re-ask (a2).

**What we need to decide.** Whether enter on the last question first opens a review of all picks, and when.

**The review view (proposed).** Enter on the last question opens a confirm state in the same card:

  ╭─ ? coordinator asks · confirm ──────────────╮
  │ g1 close    → Close both                    │
  │ dev-main PR → Open now                      │
  │ Manager     → pi + DeepSeek                 │
  │                                             │
  │ enter send · ↑↓ question to change · x drop │
  ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────╯

enter there sends. ↑↓ highlights a question, enter on it goes back to that question to change the pick or the note. x and J/K keep their meanings.

| Choice | Answer | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (REC) | Review on every card | One rule: the send enter always first shows the review. Notes and multi-picks visible at send time | Every answer costs one extra enter |
| B | Review only on cards with 2+ questions | One-question cards keep one-enter send | The send enter behaves differently by card shape |
| C | No review, as today | No change | The a1 mistake path stays |

Interrogate: ignore the whole .hive directory. Round 4. This request flips an intentional design, so here is what it touches.

## How it works today

- .gitignore ignores everything with the allowlist pattern, then allows .hive/README.md and all of .hive/spec/ (the feature specs, task briefs, evidence, and the design boards).
- Two tests enforce that: TestHomeMarkerIsTracked (a clone needs the marker, so hive never creates a home in a fresh checkout) and TestFeatureSpecPathsAreNotIgnored.
- The spec-task flow is built on git: worktree create refuses a spec task when the brief path is ignored ("path is ignored ... must allow .hive/spec/", internal/worktree/create.go:164), and it tells the agent to add !.hive/spec/ rules to the project .gitignore (internal/agent/brief.go:19). That is how qmeter and stenographer got their committed .hive/spec trees.
- Task branches merge briefs, evidence, VERIFIED.md, and the design goldens into dev. Tests read the goldens from .hive/spec/tui-v2/design/.

So "ignore all of .hive" cannot be a two-line change: git would stop delivering briefs to worktrees, and the tests would fail by design.

## 1. Where should the spec tree live?

- A (REC): move it out of .hive to spec/ at the repo root. The whole .hive directory keeps only runtime state and becomes fully ignored, including the marker. Specs, briefs, evidence, and design boards stay tracked at spec/... The change is a path rename in task create, worktree create, the tests, the skills, AGENTS.md, and git history (git mv). Every existing flow (brief delivery, evidence commits, golden checks) keeps working.
- B: keep .hive/spec paths and stop tracking: the files stay untracked, every spec commit needs git add -f, both tests flip, and worktree create gains the -f path. The repos keep carrying .hive trees once a task commits them, so your project repos would still contain .hive/spec in history.
- C: the state store owns briefs, evidence, and design boards, and git never sees them. The largest change: worktree create copies briefs in, verify reads VERIFIED.md from the state, and the design goldens move to testdata.

## 2. In your other projects, what happens?

Today hive tasks commit spec trees (and .gitignore rules) into qmeter and stenographer.

| Choice | Answer | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (REC) | Specs are normal repo content: the flow moves from .hive/spec/ to spec/ there too | One rule everywhere; spec history stays in each repo | qmeter and stenographer carry a spec/ tree |
| B | Hive state owns them there: no spec commits in project repos | Their repos stay clean of spec trees | The task flow forks: home uses spec/, projects use state delivery |
